This was the same known environmental quirk documented earlier in the campaign. Recovered via git checkout -- .worker-manifest.json (discarding the stray stale diff) followed by git checkout -B claude/yoma-rashi-audit-h5woht origin/main, confirming VERSION 15.299 and HEAD abc4bda (the just-merged 53a commit) before proceeding.

Applied the full established methodology from the start: the packet's raw-line block was parsed PROGRAMMATICALLY (python3 re.match per numbered line) before drafting build_53b_translations.py's ENTRIES list. Live-fetched Sefaria API v3 Rashi_on_Yoma.53b (hebrew version): 17 positions, matching the packet's 17 legal ids exactly in order (position count == id count, the same structural confirmation used on 53a). Derived line-to-id boundaries via the same normalize-and-substring-search script used on 53a (stripping citation-format differences to route around Sefaria's own '(ויקרא טז:טז)' vs. the packet's plain '(ויקרא טז)').

A genuine ambiguity surfaced and was resolved deliberately rather than guessed: Sefaria's own position data bundles the dibbur 'וכך היה מונה - בגמרא מפרש טעמא' ('and so he would count - the Gemara will explain the reason') as the FIRST sub-item under the SAME position label as l40's 'al haparochet' comment, even though this exact phrase ('וכך היה מונה') recurs verbatim in the base text at three separate places (l33, l36, and l40). Running a per-sub-dibbur (not per-bundled-position) search against the raw-line running text showed this note's own physical position in the printed Rashi column sits BETWEEN l33's own comment (ending at raw line 31, 'לא ידעתי לשונו:') and l36's own comment (beginning at raw line 32, 'נטל דם הפר תחילה'), i.e. print-adjacent to both, not adjacent to l40 at all. Since the note is a generic promissory comment about a counting style that recurs in all three locations, and it sits physically on the boundary between l33 and l36 (not l40, despite Sefaria's own label), I resolved this as a genuine two-way straddle linking raw lines 31-32 to BOTH l33 and l36 (the two ids the note is print-adjacent to), rather than trusting Sefaria's own position-label assignment (l40) or guessing. This is documented here as a deliberate judgment call grounded in the raw line's own physical position and the packet's own semantic-matching rule (match against segment text, never by position), not an unresolved uncertainty requiring escalation.

audit_rashi_semantic.py 53b --profile --json was run immediately after the first build pass, BEFORE the full worker:verify. First pass found ONE shift candidate: the 'Tehillim' (Psalms) anchor token appears on raw line 15 in the Hebrew, but my first-draft English had moved the word 'Psalms' to line 16 alongside the '16)' citation number. Fixed by splitting the citation across lines 15-16 exactly as the raw Hebrew does (line 15 ends '...(Psalms', line 16 begins '16).'), matching the lesson from 6a: re-derive from the raw line boundary rather than patch by guesswork. Second pass: classification ALIGNED, 4/4 anchors found (Tehillim L15, Sotah L21, dafnum 48b L21, Vayikra L38), maxAbsOffset 0, 0 shift candidates.

Live-fetched Sefaria confirmed 2 of the 17 legal ids get zero Rashi commentary on this daf: l25 (the Mishnah's own even-ha-shetiya height/coal-pan clause, self-explanatory) and l45 (R. Shimon bar Yochai's 'lo yivater davar' derivation, self-explanatory). These match Sefaria's own 2 empty array positions exactly (a clean count match).

The daf's final raw line (50, 'kol,' truncated) was linked to l47 per boundary policy, confirmed via 54a's own opening (which continues 'kol' into 'hadarah,' Lamentations 1:6, 'all her glory' - consistent with the already-corrected 54a L1 citation fix made earlier in this campaign).

Twelve raw lines needed multi-id straddle links: 11 two-way straddles (lines 2, 3, 9, 12, 18, 24, 31, 32, 36, 43, 45) and 1 three-way straddle (line 16, closing l13's Psalms citation, containing all of l16's two-word comment, and opening l19's comment, all on the same physical raw line). Per the 40b lesson, audit_rashi_association.py's multi_link count (12) was checked against my own predicted straddle count (11 double + 1 triple) before proceeding: declared_associations=63=38*1+11*2+1*3, matching my hand computation exactly.

Content covers: Rav Yosef's blindness and the honorific irony of 'may your head be raised' (spoken to a blind man about becoming head of the yeshiva), the three-steps-backward prayer-exit practice and its comparison to a dog returning to its vomit, the right-hand/left-hand symbolism debate (Rava correcting Abaye that the 'right hand' facing a person praying is the Holy One's right, not the person's own), the HP's brief exit prayer (rain, prosperity, no interruption of Davidic kingship, no dependence on charity, prayers of travelers not being answered against those praying for rain), R. Chanina ben Dosa's rain-stopping and rain-restoring prayers, the one HP who prayed too long and was met by his fellow priests, the Mishnah's account of the even ha-shetiya and its three-finger-breadth height, the counting formula for the sprinklings (bull and goat blood, inner and outer, R. Yehuda's single-stand position), and the beginning of the Gemara's discussion of where the Ark was hidden or exiled (R. Eliezer's Babylon view, R. Shimon bar Yochai's Babylon view via a different verse, R. Yehuda's hidden-in-place view, and Ulla's report of R. Matya ben Charash's question to R. Shimon bar Yochai in Rome), truncating mid-word into 54a's continuation of the second verse.
